origin: Eight original synthetic problems, authored for Blindspot. Old exam archetypes were inspiration only.

problems.title: Localising a quantum particle
problems.question: On the real line, a particle has wavefunction ψ(x) = A exp(−βx²), with β > 0 and real A > 0. Find A, ⟨x⟩, ⟨x²⟩ and the position uncertainty σₓ.
problems.assumptions: x ∈ ℝ; β > 0; A is chosen positive. All integrals are over the real line.

steps.label: Normalisation integral
steps.text: Evaluate the integral of the unnormalised probability density.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(1, 2), Pow(Integer(2), Rational(1, 2)), Pow(pi, Rational(1, 2)), Pow(Symbol('beta', positive=True), Rational(-1, 2)))

steps.label: Normalisation constant
steps.text: Impose unit total probability and choose the positive root.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Pow(Integer(2), Rational(1, 4)), Pow(pi, Rational(-1, 4)), Pow(Symbol('beta', positive=True), Rational(1, 4)))

steps.label: Mean position
steps.text: Integrate x times the normalised density; the integrand is odd.
steps.display_ast: Integer(0)

steps.label: Second moment
steps.text: Integrate x² times the normalised probability density.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(1, 4), Pow(Symbol('beta', positive=True), Integer(-1)))

steps.label: Position uncertainty
steps.text: Take the square root of the variance ⟨x²⟩ − ⟨x⟩².
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(1, 2), Pow(Symbol('beta', positive=True), Rational(-1, 2)))

problems.title: A nonlinear initial-value problem
problems.question: Solve dy/dx = (3x² + 2x)y² with y(0) = 1, on −1/4 < x < 1/4. Use separation of variables and give the branch satisfying the initial condition.
problems.assumptions: −1/4 < x < 1/4; the selected solution is positive and finite. C is a real integration constant.

steps.label: Separate variables
steps.text: Divide the differential equation by y² on the positive branch.
steps.display_ast: Add(Mul(Integer(3), Pow(Symbol('x', real=True), Integer(2))), Mul(Integer(2), Symbol('x', real=True)))

steps.label: Integrate the left side
steps.text: Find an antiderivative with respect to y, with its constant absorbed into C.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Pow(Symbol('y', positive=True), Integer(-1)))

steps.label: Integrate the right side
steps.text: Integrate the polynomial in x and introduce the integration constant.
steps.display_ast: Add(Symbol('C', real=True), Pow(Symbol('x', real=True), Integer(3)), Pow(Symbol('x', real=True), Integer(2)))
steps.mutation_note: Error mutations are excluded: changing an arbitrary integration constant can preserve the solution family without being a scalar identity.

steps.label: Apply the initial value
steps.text: Substitute x = 0 and y = 1 to fix the constant.
steps.display_ast: Integer(-1)

steps.label: Isolate the solution
steps.text: Solve for y on the specified interval.
steps.display_ast: Pow(Add(Mul(Integer(-1), Pow(Symbol('x', real=True), Integer(3))), Mul(Integer(-1), Pow(Symbol('x', real=True), Integer(2))), Integer(1)), Integer(-1))

problems.title: Two power-law modes
problems.question: Solve x²y″ − 2xy′ − 4y = 0 for x > 0, with y(1) = 3 and y′(1) = 2. Use a power-law trial solution.
problems.assumptions: x > 0; r, C₁ and C₂ are real. The trial function is xʳ.

steps.label: Substitute a power law
steps.text: Insert y = xʳ into the differential operator and divide by xʳ.
steps.display_ast: Add(Pow(Symbol('r', real=True), Integer(2)), Mul(Integer(-1), Integer(3), Symbol('r', real=True)), Integer(-4))

steps.label: Factor the indicial polynomial
steps.text: Write the indicial polynomial in factored form; its roots determine the two modes.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Add(Symbol('r', real=True), Integer(-4)), Add(Symbol('r', real=True), Integer(1)))

steps.label: Combine the modes
steps.text: Use the two distinct roots to form the general solution.
steps.display_ast: Add(Mul(Symbol('C1', real=True), Pow(Symbol('x', positive=True), Integer(4))), Mul(Symbol('C2', real=True), Pow(Symbol('x', positive=True), Integer(-1))))
steps.mutation_note: Error mutations are excluded: changing an arbitrary integration constant can preserve the solution family without being a scalar identity.

steps.label: Determine the growing mode
steps.text: Solve C₁ + C₂ = 3 and 4C₁ − C₂ = 2 for C₁.
steps.display_ast: Integer(1)

steps.label: Apply both conditions
steps.text: Substitute both constants into the general solution.
steps.display_ast: Add(Pow(Symbol('x', positive=True), Integer(4)), Mul(Integer(2), Pow(Symbol('x', positive=True), Integer(-1))))

problems.title: Driving a viscoelastic solid
problems.question: A Kelvin–Voigt solid obeys η de/dt + G e = σ₀ cos(ωt), with G, η, σ₀, ω > 0. After transients have decayed, set e(t) = A cos(ωt) + B sin(ωt). Determine A, B and the steady periodic strain.
problems.assumptions: G, η, σ₀ and ω are positive; t, A and B are real. Transients are excluded.

steps.label: Cosine balance
steps.text: Substitute the strain ansatz and collect the cosine coefficient on the left of the constitutive equation.
steps.display_ast: Add(Mul(Symbol('A', real=True), Symbol('G', positive=True)), Mul(Symbol('B', real=True), Symbol('eta', positive=True), Symbol('omega', positive=True)))

steps.label: Sine balance
steps.text: Collect the sine coefficient on the left of the constitutive equation.
steps.display_ast: Add(Mul(Integer(-1), Symbol('A', real=True), Symbol('eta', positive=True), Symbol('omega', positive=True)), Mul(Symbol('B', real=True), Symbol('G', positive=True)))

steps.label: In-phase amplitude
steps.text: Match cosine and sine coefficients to σ₀ and zero, then solve for A.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Symbol('G', positive=True), Symbol('sigma0', positive=True), Pow(Add(Pow(Symbol('G', positive=True), Integer(2)), Mul(Pow(Symbol('eta', positive=True), Integer(2)), Pow(Symbol('omega', positive=True), Integer(2)))), Integer(-1)))

steps.label: Quadrature amplitude
steps.text: Solve the same two balance equations for B.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Symbol('eta', positive=True), Symbol('omega', positive=True), Symbol('sigma0', positive=True), Pow(Add(Pow(Symbol('G', positive=True), Integer(2)), Mul(Pow(Symbol('eta', positive=True), Integer(2)), Pow(Symbol('omega', positive=True), Integer(2)))), Integer(-1)))

steps.label: Periodic strain
steps.text: Insert both amplitudes into the strain ansatz.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Symbol('sigma0', positive=True), Pow(Add(Pow(Symbol('G', positive=True), Integer(2)), Mul(Pow(Symbol('eta', positive=True), Integer(2)), Pow(Symbol('omega', positive=True), Integer(2)))), Integer(-1)), Add(Mul(Symbol('G', positive=True), cos(Mul(Symbol('omega', positive=True), Symbol('t', real=True)))), Mul(Symbol('eta', positive=True), Symbol('omega', positive=True), sin(Mul(Symbol('omega', positive=True), Symbol('t', real=True))))))

problems.title: Where is the particle most likely?
problems.question: A spherically symmetric bound-state radial function is R(r) = N r² exp(−r/(3a)), for r ≥ 0 and a > 0. The angular part has unit norm. Find the most probable radius for a radial measurement. You need not determine N.
problems.assumptions: a > 0 and N > 0. The radial density is P(r) = r²|R(r)|². Use r > 0 when differentiating log P.

steps.label: Include the volume factor
steps.text: Define q(r) = P(r)/N² and include the radial volume factor.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Pow(Symbol('r', positive=True), Integer(6)), exp(Mul(Integer(-1), Rational(2, 3), Pow(Symbol('a', positive=True), Integer(-1)), Symbol('r', positive=True))))

steps.label: Differentiate the log density
steps.text: For positive r, use the logarithmic derivative to locate a stationary point.
steps.display_ast: Add(Mul(Integer(6), Pow(Symbol('r', positive=True), Integer(-1))), Mul(Integer(-1), Rational(2, 3), Pow(Symbol('a', positive=True), Integer(-1))))

steps.label: Locate the stationary point
steps.text: Set the logarithmic derivative to zero and solve for r.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(9), Symbol('a', positive=True))

steps.label: Check the maximum
steps.text: Evaluate the second log derivative at the stationary point. Since q tends to zero at both endpoints and has one positive stationary point, it is the global maximum.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Rational(2, 27), Pow(Symbol('a', positive=True), Integer(-2)))

problems.title: A cubic angular-momentum state
problems.question: Let ψ(x,y) = (x − iy)³. Apply L_z = −iℏ(x ∂/∂y − y ∂/∂x) and determine whether ψ is an eigenfunction, and if so its eigenvalue. Normalisation is not required.
problems.assumptions: x and y are real Cartesian coordinates; ℏ > 0. The polynomial is an operator test function, not a normalisable state on all space.

steps.label: Differentiate in x
steps.text: Differentiate the cubic test function with respect to x.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(3), Pow(Add(Symbol('x', real=True), Mul(Integer(-1), I, Symbol('y', real=True))), Integer(2)))

steps.label: Differentiate in y
steps.text: Differentiate the same test function with respect to y.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Integer(3), I, Pow(Add(Symbol('x', real=True), Mul(Integer(-1), I, Symbol('y', real=True))), Integer(2)))

steps.label: Form the orbital derivative
steps.text: Combine the two partial derivatives in the order specified by L_z.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Integer(3), I, Pow(Add(Symbol('x', real=True), Mul(Integer(-1), I, Symbol('y', real=True))), Integer(3)))

steps.label: Apply the operator prefactor
steps.text: Multiply the orbital derivative by −iℏ.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Integer(3), Symbol('hbar', positive=True), Pow(Add(Symbol('x', real=True), Mul(Integer(-1), I, Symbol('y', real=True))), Integer(3)))

steps.label: Read the eigenvalue
steps.text: Identify the constant multiplying the original polynomial.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Integer(3), Symbol('hbar', positive=True))

problems.title: Energy of a shaped well state
problems.question: In an infinite well 0 < x < L, a particle of mass m has ψ(x) = N sin³(πx/L), with N > 0. Normalise the state, expand it using φₙ = √(2/L) sin(nπx/L), and calculate ⟨E⟩. You may use sin³θ = (3 sin θ − sin 3θ)/4 and Eₙ = n²π²ℏ²/(2mL²).
problems.assumptions: L, m and ℏ are positive. The wavefunction vanishes outside the well. φₙ are orthonormal.

steps.label: Integrate the density
steps.text: Integrate the square of the unnormalised state from 0 to L.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(5, 16), Symbol('L', positive=True))

steps.label: Normalise the wavefunction
steps.text: Choose the positive normalisation constant.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(4, 5), Pow(Integer(5), Rational(1, 2)), Pow(Symbol('L', positive=True), Rational(-1, 2)))

steps.label: Project onto the first mode
steps.text: Use the given trigonometric identity and the normalised eigenfunctions to extract c₁.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(3, 10), Pow(Integer(10), Rational(1, 2)))

steps.label: Project onto the third mode
steps.text: Extract c₃ from the same expansion; all other coefficients vanish.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Integer(-1), Rational(1, 10), Pow(Integer(10), Rational(1, 2)))

steps.label: Take the energy expectation
steps.text: Weight the first and third energy levels by their squared expansion amplitudes.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(9, 10), Pow(pi, Integer(2)), Pow(Symbol('L', positive=True), Integer(-2)), Pow(Symbol('hbar', positive=True), Integer(2)), Pow(Symbol('m', positive=True), Integer(-1)))

problems.title: Two measurements, one projection
problems.question: In an orthonormal basis |a⟩, |b⟩, |c⟩, prepare |ψ⟩ = (√2|a⟩ + i√3|b⟩ + √5|c⟩)/√10. Measure M = diag(1,1,−1) using the Lüders projection rule. Given outcome +1, find the probability that a subsequent measurement of H = diag(ε,4ε,9ε), ε > 0, returns 4ε. Also find the joint probability of both outcomes.
problems.assumptions: Ideal projective measurements; use the Lüders rule within the degenerate M = +1 subspace. ε > 0; no intervening evolution.

steps.label: Probability of the first outcome
steps.text: Add the populations in the a and b basis states.
steps.display_ast: Rational(1, 2)

steps.label: Renormalise the projection
steps.text: Multiply the projected state by the inverse square root of its squared norm.
steps.display_ast: Pow(Integer(2), Rational(1, 2))

steps.label: Conditional b amplitude
steps.text: Apply this multiplier to the original b amplitude; the c component is removed.
steps.display_ast: Mul(Rational(1, 5), Pow(Integer(15), Rational(1, 2)), I)

steps.label: Conditional energy probability
steps.text: Take the squared magnitude of the b amplitude after projection.
steps.display_ast: Rational(3, 5)

steps.label: Joint probability
steps.text: Multiply the first-outcome probability by the conditional energy probability.
steps.display_ast: Rational(3, 10)
